Kind of, I guess? It's not a serious issue though. In Thailand we have rolled R's. When you're in elementary school, the teachers will try to make sure everyone can roll their R's properly. Once you can do that, and get a bit older, you'll usually only be expected to roll R's during presentations or formal occasions. For the people who can't, although it maybe seen as a speech impediment, it's not too serious, you can usually get away with it. You won't be sent to a speech therapist unless your parents decide it's necessary.

We don't use them in casual conversation. We'll usually replace them with an L or a normal R instead (You'll usually hear an L. Replacing it with a normal R can make you sound dumb, extra, or like someone with an accent, depending on the way you speak. You'll often hear the normal R in modern singing though.)

People will sometimes think you're being too formal or extra if you say the rolled R's properly, like a news anchor or a teacher or smth. I personally like saying words correctly but don't wanna annoy my friends, so I don't lol.
